srep-0041-shadow-catcher-opacity.rule: SREP 41 s3-4: geometry: light (320,-100,150) down, floor y=300 (400 px), caster top face y=90 half-width 20 -> shadow half-width 20*400/190 = 42.105 px: x 277.895..362.105, ortho camera 1 px/unit; alpha = 0.5*(1-0) = 0.5; C' = C(1-alpha) in linear light (CONVENTIONS 1.4: colours are decoded before compositing): lin(128)=0.2159 -> 0.1079 -> sRGB 92.4

srep-0041-shadow-catcher-ambient.rule: SREP 41 s2-4 with D11: geometry: light (320,-100,150) down, floor y=300 (400 px), caster top face y=90 half-width 20 -> shadow half-width 20*400/190 = 42.105 px: x 277.895..362.105, ortho camera 1 px/unit; ambient 0.18 white (A=0.18, D11: I*c_diff); spot E=3*(100/d)^2, L=(1-F0)*E*n.l with F0=0.04 (D11 as corrected 2026-10-06: f*E*n.l, f=(1-F)c/pi, no factor pi), view and light along the normal; in shadow ratio=A/(A+L) ~ 0.76 (L=0.96*E*n.l/pi), C'=lin(128)*ratio, sRGB-encoded; per-region mean of the per-pixel values; per-pixel means over the four shadow regions 112.77 to 112.79 (computed with the corrected D11), so 113 within the kit tolerance of 3 code values; before the D11 correction the derivation gave 93 with the factor pi in L, and the engine renders 113

srep-0041-shadow-catcher-nolight-shadow.rule: SREP 41 s6: the only light has castShadow=false: v=1, E_sh=E_un, alpha=0 on the whole catcher: the plate is unchanged (128) in every strip, inside the would-be shadow too

srep-0051-wiggle-corner-vertex-340.rule: SREP 51, Semantics: "The vertices are the same points in both modes". The vertices of the wiggled path (detail 3 per hundred units over 200 units, so one every 40 px from x = 220) are x = 220, 260, 300, 340, ...; at the vertex x = 340 the corner polyline (no mode) and the smooth spline pass through the same point, so the red centroid in the 4 px slab 338..342 has the same height as in the smooth case srep-0051-wiggle-smooth-vertex-340 (cy 216.44). Only cy is asserted: the slab holds the segments on both sides of the vertex, whose slopes differ between the two modes. The claim is the equality of the two cases; the value is the engine-seeded noise of seed 7 (a regression pin shared with the smooth case). Not yet measured on the engine.
